newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates steady, focus on 3-month.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates steady, focus on 3-month.

text.p: Interbank rates were generally steady on Tuesday with early activity confined to three-month money, dealers said.
"There's a bit of interest in the three-month. But the market remains generally quiet though rates are quite stable," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
But rates could be pressured again with more funds coming into the market, dealers said.
They said there will be maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit on Friday and a 900-million ringgit long-term government bond issue on May 15.
A 420-million ringgit long term government bond issue and a 500-million ringgit Bank Negara bills issue had matured last week. They were not rolled over.
"Unless Bank Negara issues fresh bills or MGS, rates should start coming off again," said another dealer.
Dealers said rumours that the central bank will announce a new Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) issue had prevented lenders from offering lower and kept interbank rates steady.
One-week and two-week money was at 6.8/7.0 percent against 6.9/7.1 on Monday, and three-week was at 7.00/10 percent against 7.10/20.
One-month money at 7.25/30 percent, three-month at 7.30/35 and six-month at 7.35/40, were all unchanged.
The overnight interbank rate is expected to remain between 6.5 and 7.0 percent, dealers said.
It closed on Monday at 6.70/80 percent.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were generally higher.
At 0300 GMT, the benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up two points at 92.69, or an implied yield of 7.31 percent.
December rose three to 92.69, or 7.31 percent.
March and June 1998 were up four each to 92.62 and 92.60, or 7.38 and 7.40 percent respectively.
